transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], Hive-Touched Pack [T-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain needles down on Hollowmoot's last dry causeway as a woman half-runs, half-wades toward you, skirts sodden black to the knee — Sela, who kept the eel-traps below Wick Lane until three nights ago. Her boy Corren followed a sound none of the rest of you can hear out past the reed banks toward Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, and hasn't come back. Behind her, the causeway itself is dying: the water already licks the third plank-step down, and by the old marks on the pilings, Gullet Ford will be underwater by tomorrow's low tide — your last one for weeks. Out past the reeds, something moves in a loose, patient line, low to the water, in no hurry at all; hooked shapes catch what little light there is. Sela grabs whichever of you stands nearest and won't let go.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Hush. I've got you, and you're going to tell me everything. What did Corren follow into those reeds? What sound made him leave?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde catches Sela's trembling hands and holds her steady, meeting her eyes with the focused attention that has made a dozen desperate people trust her across night-barge tables. She doesn't pull away from the fear—she leans into it, solid and present.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Sela, stay with me. When did Corren slip away? Which way did he go—toward the temple, or into the deep reeds?

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (I grip Sela's shoulders firmly, meeting her panicked eyes through the driving rain. My gaze flickers once toward the hooked shapes moving in the reeds, then locks back on her face—steady, present.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Your son is taken by the hive-touched, but I know how to fight what took him—that's what I'm for.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen lets Sela's grip hold, eyes fixed on the shapes moving through the reeds with their hooked spears and patient, coordinated hunger. She reaches into the years the Order spent training her, into the bitter certainty of her childhood—that knowledge of how the hive-touched move, hunt, think. She's reading their patterns now, feeling the cadence of their wrongness like a spider reading vibrations on its web, preparing herself for what comes next.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Easy, Sela. I've got you—you're on solid plank now. Tell me what you saw out there. What took the boy?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire catches Sela with a firm grip that grounds her, drawing on her training in the watch drills. She holds the line of the causeway with her body, steady and present, while her trained eye scans the reeds and the water beyond, counting the threat and marking the shapes that catch the light. She keeps Sela close but doesn't let her panic—there's work to understand first.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Threshwick was just one mill-house—this is your son. I was trained for this, Sela, and I won't fail where the Order taught me to stand. Let me see what we're facing.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Will: dice 0 - - -, invoking Orphan of the first outbreak, raised in the Order's care [MO-A1], Exorcist Who Doubts the Hive Has Souls [MO-HC] → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
Sela's words come in a flood, matching the rain: "The bell — Saint Orrin's bell, ringing wrong, like it's underwater and singing anyway. Corren just... walked. Toward the temple, past the ford, out where the reeds get tall." She doesn't let go of whichever hand holds hers, knuckles white.

Morwen doesn't blink at the approaching shapes. Years of Order drilling click into place behind her eyes — the pack doesn't hunt like beasts, and it doesn't hunt like men. It hunts in a *rhythm*, spears lifting and falling in near-unison, like a congregation moving through a rite it no longer remembers the meaning of. She reads the pattern whole: where the gaps fall, when they close, how the ignored pain makes them slow to change direction once committed. It settles into her like doctrine — cold, useful, certain. The others feel it too, in how she suddenly stands straighter, voice low: "I know how they move. Watch the second beat — that's when they overcommit."

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Hold the line or get Sela higher. When the pack commits on Morwen's second beat, we move through the gap.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde releases Sela's hands and steps forward, her attention pivoting from comfort to tactical clarity. She reads the whole group in a glance—the same sharp empathy that's kept desperate people alive across night-barge tables—assessing who can hold and how they fit against what's coming. Her voice drops to that focused certainty that cuts through panic.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Listen to me, Sela—the rain speaks to those who listen. We have until dawn, when low tide brings our window. We reach him before then or lose everyone.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (I close my eyes against the rain for just a breath and listen. Every drop carries the flood's voice—its patterns, its rhythm. The causeway trembles as water climbs higher, and I read the story the deluge tells: how long it will hold, when it will release. When my eyes open, they're steady on Sela's face. I'm still gripping her shoulder, holding the line.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The second beat—that's when they break. I'm going through there now.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward into the driving rain with absolute certainty, eyes locked on the moving shapes in the reeds. She's read their pattern like scripture—the moment when their hive-coordination falters, when the spears commit and can't be withdrawn. She moves toward them with the cold, purposeful intensity of someone the Order trained from childhood to hunt what feeds on the hive's wrongness. No hesitation. No doubt.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: We hold here on the causeway. They come single file, and their nets are worthless. Every step down this approach costs them blood.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire draws on her training from the Order's orphanage—the watch drills drilled into her bones—and on everything in her that refuses to break. She traces the terrain with a tactical eye: the bottlenecks, the high ground, the narrow approach where the pack's numbers become useless. Her hand steadies on her weapon. She has held this line before. She'll hold it now.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Not one of them gets past. Not while I'm standing here.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Empathy: dice - + - + → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 + 0 0 → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Fight: dice - - 0 +, invoking Exorcist's Certainty [A-1.1.1] → Good (+3) vs Good (+3): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Fight: dice 0 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen reads the second beat exactly right and drives her strike home as a spear-hand overcommits — but the lunge carries her three steps past Mire's chokepoint, out onto open, slick planking where the rest of the pack can close around her before she can pull back.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde's voice cuts through the rain like a knife through rope — in one glance she's read the whole group's footing, their reach, the gaps between them, and suddenly everyone knows exactly where to stand (**The Group Stands Ready**). Aldous, eyes still shut, feels the flood's rhythm settle into certainty: there's a window, narrow and true, when the water pulls back before it rises for good (**The Low Tide Window**). Mire plants herself at the chokepoint, and in a heartbeat the causeway itself becomes a weapon — narrow planks, deep water on both sides, a killing lane the pack's numbers can't help them in (**Control the Causeway**). Morwen reads the second beat exactly right, drives her strike through the overcommitted spear-arm and *connects* — bone cracks, the hive-touched staggers — but her own momentum carries her three long strides past Mire's line, out onto slick open planking where the rest of the pack is already closing the gap around her, hooked spears rising on all sides.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: You're pinned! Look here—look at me, you hunger-drunk things! Here!

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde uses the rain and chaos as cover, moving low and quick along the slick planking. She slides up behind the left flank of the pack—the spear-carrier whose attention is locked wholly on Morwen. She strikes at what a cook knows: the soft places, the places where things stop moving, the junction of jaw and neck where she read the coordination seeming to originate.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: She's not yours to take. I'm marked by the flood—come for me instead!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous rushes across the slick causeway planks, moving fast through the needling rain. He throws himself into the closing circle around Morwen, arms spread wide, putting his body between her and the rising spear-tips.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You're not a true hive—I know how to sever what binds you together.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen plants herself amid the closing spears and reaches for the spiritual certainty the Order drilled into her bones since childhood. She fixes her will on the fractures in their hive-coordination, weaponizing the isolation between each body—the chasm that separates one possessed creature from the next. Her voice drops low, speaking the rites that cut through false connections.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold position, Morwen—I'm breaking through!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire breaks from her chokepoint position as the pack's hooked spears close around Morwen, stepping forward with controlled aggression. She drives her weapon into the closest hive-touched and forces them backward, opening space and pulling their focused attention back onto herself—back toward the narrow approach where their numbers mean nothing.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — attack with Stealth: dice + - + 0 → Good (+3) vs Terrible (-2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Hive-Touched Pack taken out)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — attack with Athletics: dice - - - -, invoking The Low Tide Window [A-1.1.3] → Mediocre (+0) vs Mediocre (+0): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice - - 0 -, invoking Exorcist's Certainty [A-1.1.1], Boost: Morwen steps forward into the  [A-1.1.4] → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Hive-Touched Pack mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — attack with Fight: dice 0 0 - +, invoking Control the Causeway [A-1.1.5] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fantastic (+6): TIE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous throws himself into the ring of spears and gets his body between Morwen and the pack — but a hooked spear catches his coat as he crashes past, and he goes down hard on the slick planking, momentarily tangled and open, the flood's warning window he read a moment ago already narrowing.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mire's blade drives the hive-touched back a step and reopens the killing lane, but her thrust overextends past the chokepoint's edge — for a breath she's standing in open water past the pilings, exposed to whatever else the flood is hiding, before she wrenches herself back to solid planking.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde's blade finds the hollow beneath a jaw and the spear-carrier drops mid-stride, and something in the whole loose line of them stutters — the second beat Morwen named breaks apart into panic and stumbling retreat, hooked spears clattering as the pack scatters back into the reeds, hive-song silenced for now. Morwen's rite lands home on the one still standing, a shudder running through it like a rope cut mid-pull, and it folds, thrashing, into the black water. Aldous goes down hard where the spear caught his coat, tangled on open planking for one long breath with no one closing on him now — he comes up soaked, bruised, and laughing with relief he can't quite hide. Mire wrenches herself back from the open water past the pilings, and just before her boots find solid pilewood again, something vast and patient brushes past her calf beneath the surface — gone before she can name it, but she felt the size of it, and it wasn't the hive. Sela's sobbing has turned to something closer to hope: the causeway is clear, the low tide window still stands, and the road to Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple lies open ahead of you.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sela won't be talked into staying behind — she wades in ahead of you, skirts heavy, calling Corren's name into the rain until Ysolde has to physically slow her. Beyond the causeway the world turns to reed and black water: old pilings from some drowned road still mark a line through it, if you can read them right, but the mats of reed between them hide ground that isn't ground at all — Aldous's boot sinks past the ankle testing the first step and comes up with a wet, sucking reluctance. Somewhere out past the reeds, low and rhythmic, the swarm-song from the belltower carries across the water, and closer than that, unhurried and enormous, something shoulders a wake through the channel that has nothing to do with wind.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: We go together, Sela. Watch my steps, and hold on. Your boy called you here—I'll get us to him.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde catches Sela's hand firmly and meets her eyes—that focused attention that's kept desperate people alive across night-barge tables. She doesn't fight the panic; she reads it, channels it into forward motion. Hand in hand, she begins testing the ground ahead, reading the reeds like she reads scared people: finding the solid places, the routes to safety.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain's warning me of dangers ahead, Sela. Hold to me and let me guide you—your son needs you alive.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (I surge through the sucking marsh to catch Sela's wrist, pulling her firmly back from plunging deeper into dark water. My boots sink past the ankle with each step, but I've already felt the rhythm of this flood in my bones. I keep her close, moving carefully, my eyes narrowed against the needling rain as I read the shapes beneath the surface. Something vast moves in the deeper channels—patient and enormous—but I focus on Sela's arm in my grip, guiding her forward step by measured step.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: There's something vast moving beneath us—not hive-touched, something else. Sela, slow down. Let me read what it wants before we stumble into its jaws.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen moves deeper into the reeds, body tense, eyes tracking the massive disturbance carving through the black water. The years of Order training click into place—she's reading this new threat the same way she read the hive-touched pack, cataloging its speed, its path, its hunger. Whatever moves beneath them is patient and deliberate, and she means to understand what it wants before it surfaces.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold here a moment. I felt something down there—something vast and nothing like the pack. Before we follow Sela into that water, I need to know what hunts these channels.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire stops at the edge of the causeway and raises her hand in warning before Sela can wade deeper. She's still feeling the memory of that vast, patient shape brushing past her calf in the black water—something that wasn't the hive-touched, something far larger. Now she turns her full attention to the reed-channels ahead, eyes tracking the pilings and reading where the water moves unnaturally, where something has carved a hunting corridor. She applies the focus the watch drills drilled into her bones, building a map of what moves in those shallows and marking safe channels between.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The old training runs too deep. I need to see what we're facing—truly see it—before we wade Sela into its jaws.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Empathy: dice - 0 + 0, invoking Exiled Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything [YS-HC] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Notice: dice + 0 - + → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 - + +, invoking Raised in the Order's orphanage, trained to the watch drills [MI-A1] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
Ysolde threads her fingers through Sela's and doesn't let the woman's panic set the pace — instead she reads the reed-mats the way she reads a frightened face, feeling for the give that means mud and the resistance that means piling underneath. Step by step, Sela's breathing steadies to match hers, the two of them moving as one unit now, sure-footed where a moment ago there was only blind wading (**Sela Grounded, Moving Together**). Morwen's eyes never leave the water's surface, and the wake she's tracking starts to make sense — it isn't random; it circles wide, tests, withdraws, comes back tighter, hunting by feel rather than sight, patient in a way that tells her exactly how not to feed it (**Read the Threat's Pattern**). Mire's trained eye finishes the map: the vast shape favors the deeper channels between the old pilings, avoiding the shallow ground over the firm line, which means the safest crossing is also the one that keeps you closest to where it swims — a bargain, not a rescue. The belltower's swarm-song rises and falls somewhere ahead through the rain, patient as the thing in the water, and the low tide window Aldous felt is already narrowing.

You have your line across the mire now, and you know the shape of what's hunting it. The question is whether you can hold the pace Sela needs and still keep clear of the water's patient circles before the tide turns against you.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Stay with me, Sela. One step, then the next. Your son needs you alive at that temple, and I'm not letting the marsh take either of us.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde keeps Sela's hand firm in hers, reading the minute shifts in the woman's breathing—where the panic wants to spike, where exhaustion threatens to pull her under. She adjusts their pace to what Sela can hold without breaking, calls back to Aldous and Morwen with quiet, cutting authority. "Hold the line. We move together." Each step is deliberate, grounded, and her own steadiness flows into Sela like a tide pulling back from the shore. She doesn't rush. She doesn't let them stop. She reads the marsh the way she reads frightened people at a night-barge table—finding the solid places, avoiding the give that means drowning.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The ghosts that mark me—they remember these channels. Stay close to me, Sela, and we'll find Corren before the water rises for good.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous continues forward with studied care, guiding Sela through the marsh with a firm grip on her wrist. Though vast shapes move in the deeper waters and the rain needles down all around them, his eyes stay fixed on the patterns in the flood—reading the rhythm of the water, feeling the old paths that the drowned dead remember. He moves them forward step by measured step toward the temple's swarm-song, keeping the pace Sela needs while skirting the hungry circles of the creature beneath.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You want to feed on fear in these waters? Then face me first.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps deliberately into the deeper water where the creature circles, her voice dropping into the old rites the Order drilled into her bones since childhood. She reaches out with her will, asserting dominance over this unknown thing—not hive-touched, but something she'll still answer to herself before it hunts another soul in these waters. If it wants this channel, it answers to her first.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: You've got your path—the shallow ground's your lifeline. Watch where I step and follow it. We move together, we move fast enough, and that thing in the water stays hunting the deep channels where it can't help us.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire plants herself at the group's threshold into the reed-channels, one hand raised to hold them a breath longer while she points out the line she's read—the shallow ground over the firm pilings that runs northernmost through the reeds. Her eye tracks the vast shape's circling in the deeper channels, and she nods once, satisfied. Then she turns back to the group, weapon still in hand, and steps forward into the shallows. She moves carefully but without hesitation, testing each step before committing, calling back quietly: "Stay to the shallow line. Stay close. The thing hunts by feel—we're below its weight if we stay the course.")

transcript.text: Ysolde's steadiness works — Sela's breathing evens out to match hers, and the two of them cross the worst of the reed-mire as one, sure-footed, the shallow piling-line holding true beneath their feet. But out in the deep channel, Morwen's rite lands like a blow — the water shudders around the vast shape, a groan of pain rippling through it that isn't remotely human — and for one triumphant heartbeat it seems to work. Then the black water breaks open beneath her. The Pikemaw surges up in a wall of spray, jaws closing on her leg before she can wrench free, and drags her half under in a welter of blood and reed-froth. She comes up screaming, the rite unfinished, one leg torn open to the bone, the old wound from Threshwick's memory nothing beside this — the thing has marked her, deep and ugly, and it isn't done circling.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: It's mine—get her clear!

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde lets go of Sela's hand and wades into the black water without hesitation. She slides in along the Pikemaw's flank, reading it the way she reads desperate people at a night-barge table—finding the moment when hunger overrides caution. Her knife reaches for soft places, the junctions where blood flows beneath hide, ready to make herself the pressing threat that can't be ignored.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: She doesn't fall to this hunger—come for me instead, creature! I'm marked by the flood itself!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous plunges into the deeper water where the Pikemaw has dragged Morwen under, his body moving with desperate speed despite the sucking marsh. He throws himself between the creature's ancient jaws and the bleeding woman, arms outstretched, calling on the drowned ghosts that mark him to give him the strength to make this thing answer for what it's done.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I don't break—not for hunger, not for you. I've trained my whole life for this.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen wrenches herself hard against the creature's jaws, blood streaming into the black water. With the drill-sharp certainty of someone trained from childhood to hunt what feeds on wrongness, she drives her heel up toward the creature's eye socket, trying to force it to release her and buy space to move.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Not while I'm standing here!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire breaks from the shallow line without hesitation and wades into the deep channel, water churning around her legs. Her blade rises with the cold, practiced intensity the Order drilled into her bones since childhood—one perfect thrust aimed at the massive jaws holding Morwen, driving the point-blank through hide and hunger to force the creature to release its prey or answer her steel.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Not while I'm standing. You will let her go, or you will answer me.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.text: Morwen's heel finds the eye socket and the jaws loosen just enough — but the release flings her backward into deep water, her blade torn from her grip and lost to the black current, leaving her weaponless and gasping as Ysolde, Aldous, and Mire close the kill around her.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The Pikemaw thrashes once more as Aldous's dive and Mire's driving thrust find their mark together, point and current tearing through hide gone soft with Ysolde's earlier wound — the vast shape goes rigid, shudders, and rolls belly-up in a spreading cloud of black-red water before sinking into the reeds, still at last. Morwen comes up gasping in the wake of it, weaponless, her blade lost to the current, but alive — Ysolde and Mire haul her toward the shallow piling-line before the current can claim anything else. Sela, white-faced, has never let go of the reed stem she grabbed when the water broke open, and now she stares at the four of you like she's only just understanding what you're willing to wade through for a stranger's son. The rain doesn't ease, and the swarm-song from the belltower rises again now that the water's violence has passed, patient and untroubled by what just died in the channel below it — but the mire is crossed, the line to Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple lies open ahead, and the low tide window, though narrower now, still holds.

costs.text: Sela's eyes catch on Morwen's face mid-panic — she stops mid-sentence, breath hitching. 'You — you're the one from Threshwick, the one who cast the devils out of the mill-house. They said you'd come. They said you'd know how to save him.' Her grip tightens to desperate, and now she's not just a frig

As Mire plants herself at the choke point, the old fury from Wick Lane surges — she steps a half-pace past the safe line to make absolutely sure not one of them slips by, putting herself in reach of the first hooked spear.

Morwen reads the second beat exactly right and drives her strike home as a spear-hand overcommits — but the lunge carries her three steps past Mire's chokepoint, out onto open, slick planking where the rest of the pack can close around her before she can pull back.

Aldous throws himself into the ring of spears and gets his body between Morwen and the pack — but a hooked spear catches his coat as he crashes past, and he goes down hard on the slick planking, momentarily tangled and open, the flood's warning window he read a moment ago already narrowing.

Mire's blade drives the hive-touched back a step and reopens the killing lane, but her thrust overextends past the chokepoint's edge — for a breath she's standing in open water past the pilings, exposed to whatever else the flood is hiding, before she wrenches herself back to solid planking.

Driven by the old need to prove she can master any threat as surely as she once held the Wardens' line, Mire pushes past the safe run of old pilings to get a clean look at the Pikemaw's wake — and her boot finds mud with no bottom to it.

Mire abandons the shallow line entirely to close on the Pikemaw's jaws, wading past the firm piling-line into the deep channel itself — she's now standing in the creature's own hunting water, exposed to whatever else moves beneath, all reason burned away by the need to make it let Morwen go.

Morwen's heel finds the eye socket and the jaws loosen just enough — but the release flings her backward into deep water, her blade torn from her grip and lost to the black current, leaving her weaponless and gasping as Ysolde, Aldous, and Mire close the kill around her.

ambiguities.issue: The baseline rules state 'the GM may offer a compel on any player aspect or trouble.' In events 10 and 16, the Compel action's actor field is the player (Morwen, Mire) rather than 'GM', with compel_forced=false, suggesting the players self-initiated/proposed the compel on their own aspect/trouble rather than the GM offering it.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated player-proposed compels as valid GM-equivalent offers; both were logged as 'accepted' and processed normally (fp awarded per acceptance).

ambiguities.issue: The rules define two stress tracks (physical and mental) but do not specify which skills map to which track. Morwen attacks the Hive-Touched Pack using Will (events 24/30) alongside Fight/Athletics/Stealth attacks from other characters against the same NPC card (T-01), leaving it unclear whether the Will attack was meant to contribute to a mental track or the same physical track that eventually took T-01 out.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table allowed the Will attack's shifts to count toward the same conflict/track that removed T-01 from play, alongside the physical-skill attacks.

ambiguities.issue: AMB-19 establishes that a tie produces a Fate Core-style boost aspect plus a deck draw, but the baseline rules do not define who may invoke a boost created from the acting character's own complication. Morwen later invokes her own boost aspect (A-1.1.4, born from her own tie-cost at event 21) on a subsequent roll (event 30).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table allowed the character who incurred the tie complication to invoke the resulting boost aspect on their own later roll.

ambiguities.issue: Rules define fixed consequence values (mild 2, moderate 4, severe 6), but at event 53 a hit of 4 shifts (opposition +3 vs defend -1) was absorbed by taking a consequence explicitly labeled 'severe' while the field reads 'Absorb 4 physical' — a value that matches 'moderate,' not 'severe.' The rules don't say whether a player may take an over-sized consequence slot (or mislabel one) to cover a smaller hit, or whether the consequence taken must match the shift total.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the consequence as a full severe slot ('Torn by the Pikemaw') narratively, even though only 4 of its notional 6 capacity was needed to cover the hit; no lower (moderate) slot was used instead.

ambiguities.issue: Baseline rules place no limit on how many compels the GM may offer a single character within one scene/conflict. Mire was compelled twice in quick succession (events 42 and 58) during the same crossing/fight, both accepted.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table allowed both compels to stand with no cap, each independently granting +1 fate point to Mire, since the rules impose no frequency limit.

ambiguities.issue: The scene's cost/compel/fill ledger header implies compels and costs are meant to pull a card and use its tags, but none of the three recorded costs/compels (events 42, 58, 63) has a draw_id or drawn card, and the baseline rules text given to the referee is silent on when a draw is required for a compel vs. a pure improvised cost.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table let the GM improvise all three costs/compels without drawing a card, treating the draw as optional flavor rather than a mandatory step for every compel/cost.
